close_reason: MemoryBackend::query_objects now honors all 19 ContactCardFilterCondition fields (RFC 9610 §3.3.1) and all comparators (§3.3.2). Adopts the canonical mail-server Pattern G (.expect() type-identity roundtrip — silent .ok() fallback would re-introduce the match-all bug). 39 new unit tests cover every filter field; 2 new integration tests exercise the end-to-end query path. Implementation in commit 872b4ee.
description:
Trigger: any ContactCard/query call with a filter other than {inAddressBook: <id>}, or any AddressBook/query call (latter is degenerate since RFC 9610 does not define it, so not exposed via dispatcher). Also any call with a non-empty sort array.

Bad behavior: memory.rs:467-541 reads the filter ONLY to extract the inAddressBook string field (and only when O::TYPE_NAME == 'ContactCard'); every other RFC 9610 §3.3.1 filter condition (text, name, email, kind, uid, hasMember, etc.) is silently dropped and the query returns ALL objects. The _sort parameter is prefixed-underscore and never consulted, so the order returned is HashMap iteration order, not the spec-required RFC 9610 §3.3.2 deterministic sort.

This is the SAME defect class as JMAP-826m.4 (metadata-server MemoryBackend.query_objects ignores filter and sort) and JMAP-q2wa.3 (mail-server filter dispatch regression). The cookie-cutter sibling template established that silent-match-all on query is a bug, not a documented limitation.

Impact:
 - The cascade-cleanup loop documented in README (which uses 'ContactCard/query with inAddressBook filter as cleanup path before destroy') has the same vulnerability shape: a future feature that adds a stricter filter will see ALL cards selected, not just the ones in the target book, and the cleanup will over-delete.
 - Integration tests that query for specific subsets silently pass with the right contents because the empty-store check, the test data, and the silently-dropped filter all happen to make total == expected. The defect is invisible until production.

Fix: either implement the filter algebra (the FilterOperator / FilterCondition shape is already available via O::Filter) and stable sort, OR fail loudly with serverFail / a panic in debug for any non-trivial filter. Silent match-all is the worst outcome.
title: MemoryBackend.query_objects silently ignores all filters except ContactCard.inAddressBook, and all sort comparators
